one_sentence: God is proven when the deepest law of fallen creation encounters someone it cannot lawfully bind.
executive_summary: This document argues that a true proof of God cannot rest on mere rule-breaking, which could be faked by demons, magicians, or advanced intelligences. Instead, the proof must be a rightful exception: the deepest law of the fallen system (death) encountering someone it has no legal claim to bind. The key evidence is the resurrection of Christ, reframed not as a supernatural event but as a structural verdict: death had no jurisdiction over Him because He was sinless. The conclusion is that such an event proves moral authority over the final law, distinguishing God from mere power.
short_summary: This document is a philosophical-theological argument for a non-arbitrary proof of God. Its core structural claim is that God is proven when the deepest law of the fallen system (death) encounters someone it cannot lawfully bind. The key evidence is the resurrection of Christ, understood as a legal verdict rather than a mere miracle. This matters because it grounds theism in justice and authority, not just power.
